newsitem.title: SYRIA: Japanese envoy discusses Red Army suspects in Syria.
newsitem.headline: Japanese envoy discusses Red Army suspects in Syria.

text.p: A Japanese envoy on Wednesday sought Syrian support regarding the case of five Japanese detained in Lebanon as members of the Japanese Red Army, diplomats said.

Hiroshi Hirabayashi, chief foreign policy adviser for Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, told reporters after talks with Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara that he presented "ideas" to Shara on what Tokyo thinks about the Red Army suspects.
He said that Japan would wait to see what judicial measures the Lebanese government would take regarding the suspects before taking another step.
Syria is the main power broker in Lebanon where it has some 35,000 troops. The five Red Army suspects were arrested last month along with three other Asians in Lebanon.
The Red Army, founded in 1971, is allied to hardline anti-Israeli Palestinian factions.
"I explained to Mr Shara the present situation regarding the detainees in Lebanon and gave ideas on what the Japanese govrenment and the prime minister think about the issue," Hirabayashi said.
"These ideas were shaped in light of our discussion with the Lebanese government," Hirabayashi said without elaborating.
Asked about the next step that Japan would make, the envoy said: "We will wait to see what the Lebanese authorities will do before we decide our next measure."
Hirabayashi said that Japan had confirmed that five of the Asians detained in Lebanon were Red Army members.
"Their identity and their belonging to the Red Army were confirmed in Lebanon yesterday," he said.
Japanese officials said that Hirabayashi would meet Syrian President Hafez al-Assad later on Wednesday or Thursday to convey a message from the Japanese prime minister.
Hirabayashi arrived in Damascus from Beirut on Tuesday and said he was "very satisfied" with his talks there covering the case of the Red Army men.

Confusion and conflicting reports emerged after Hashimoto said in Tokyo on February 18 that Lebanese officials had told him they had arrested six Japanese suspected members of the group in Lebanon's eastern Bekaa valley.
Lebanon's foreign ministry initially confirmed the reports but later Lebanese security sources denied holding any Japanese citizens.
This week a high-ranking Lebanese judicial source said in Beirut that Lebanon was holding five Japanese Red Army guerrillas in Beirut.
